---
title: "第四章 让科学技术改善所有美国人的生活"
subtitle: "Chapter IV: Ensuring That Science and Technology Better the Lives of All Americans"
---

## IV.1 科学与技艺的联姻

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.1 The Marriage of Science and Craft</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-2-en"><p>In policy conversations, we often speak as though technology consists solely of intellectual property and gadgets. We focus on the patents that can be filed, the knowledge that can be written down, or the complex machines that can be built. But scientific and technological capability consists of much more than its most visible inputs and outputs.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-2-zh"><p>在政策讨论中，我们谈论技术时往往仿佛它只由知识产权和新奇装置构成。我们关注可以申请的专利、可以写下来的知识，或者可以造出来的复杂机器。但科学技术能力远远不止它最显眼的那些投入与产出。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-3-en"><p>A better taxonomy holds that technology exists in three forms: tools, explicit instructions, and process knowledge.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-121-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-121" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 121"><sup>121</sup></a> Consider chipmaking. The tools are the lithography machines, etchers, implanters, and more. The explicit instructions are the blueprints and recipes. But the process knowledge, like how to troubleshoot semiconductor yields, how complex variables affect wafer cleaning, how the next process node should be designed to balance performance and manufacturing risk, lives in the heads of experienced engineers and technicians.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-3-zh"><p>一个更合理的分类认为，技术以三种形态存在：工具、明确的说明书，以及工艺知识。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-121-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-121" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 121"><sup>121</sup></a> 以芯片制造为例。工具是光刻机、刻蚀机、离子注入机等等。明确的说明书是图纸和配方。而工艺知识——比如如何排查半导体良率问题、复杂的变量如何影响晶圆清洗、下一制程节点应当如何设计才能兼顾性能与制造风险——则存在于经验丰富的工程师和技术人员的头脑中。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-4-en"><p>This tacit knowledge cannot be fully codified. Anyone can be placed in front of a piano bench with a score of Rachmaninoff, but playing it well requires a personal command of musical dynamics and tactile skill.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-4-zh"><p>这种默会知识无法完全编码。任何人都可以坐到琴凳前，面前摆上一份 Rachmaninoff 的乐谱，但要弹得好，需要对音乐力度与触键技巧的个人掌控。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-5-en"><p>As the chemist-turned-philosopher Michael Polanyi observed, “we can know more than we can tell.”<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-122-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-122" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 122"><sup>122</sup></a> A skilled welder knows things about metal behavior that no manual captures, like the way aluminum warns you before it warps, or the sound a good bead makes as it forms. A machinist develops intuitions about cutting tools that come only from years at the lathe. A pharmaceutical manufacturing technician recognizes subtle variations in chemical processes that determine whether a drug batch meets specifications.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-5-zh"><p>由化学家转为哲学家的 Michael Polanyi 曾指出：「我们知道的，多于我们能说出的。」<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-122-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-122" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 122"><sup>122</sup></a> 一名熟练的焊工对金属行为的了解是任何手册都记录不下来的，比如铝在变形之前会怎样先发出预警，或者一条好的焊缝在成形时发出什么声音。机械师对刀具的直觉，只能来自车床前的多年积累。制药生产的技术员能辨别出化学过程中那些决定一批药品是否合格的细微变化。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-6-en"><p>This process knowledge, embodied in an experienced workforce, is the true keystone of technological capability.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-6-zh"><p>这种体现在有经验劳动力身上的工艺知识，才是技术能力真正的基石。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-7-en"><p>The same applies to the practice of science. When the sociologist Harry Collins studied laboratories attempting to replicate a new type of laser in the 1970s, he found that no scientist succeeded using published sources alone. Those who built working devices had all spent time in a laboratory with someone who had already done it. The knowledge to build the laser flowed through personal contact, often so subtle that scientists themselves could not fully articulate what they had learned.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-123-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-123" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 123"><sup>123</sup></a></p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-7-zh"><p>科学的实践同样如此。社会学家 Harry Collins 在 1970 年代研究那些试图复现一种新型激光器的实验室时发现，仅靠已发表的文献，没有一位科学家成功。造出可用装置的人，都曾与已经做成过的人在同一间实验室里相处过。建造激光器的知识经由人际接触传递，而且常常细微到科学家自己也说不清究竟学到了什么。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-123-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-123" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 123"><sup>123</sup></a></p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-8-en"><p>Likewise, a synthetic biologist improves through countless failed experiments while coaxing cells into expressing a novel protein. An immunologist, after years of experience and guidance from senior mentors, develops intuitions for which protocols will work with finicky cell lines, knowledge no methods section can capture. This is why many forms of scientific expertise require years of on-the-job training in working research organizations, and why academic publications alone remain insufficient to transmit the craft of science.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-8-zh"><p>同样，合成生物学家是在无数次失败实验中、在诱导细胞表达一种新蛋白的过程中长进的。免疫学家经过多年实践与资深导师的指导，才会对哪些流程能对付难伺候的细胞系形成直觉，而这种知识是任何「方法」章节都写不下来的。这就是为什么许多类型的科学专长需要在运转中的研究机构里经受多年在职训练，也是为什么仅靠学术论文不足以传授科学这门手艺。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-9-en"><p>Papers and patents are not the ultimate ends of progress, but way stations in the training of better scientists, engineers, and technicians. Science is not simply about the equipment, which any laboratory with enough capital can purchase, nor the instructions, which can be shared on a sheet of paper.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-124-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-124" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 124"><sup>124</sup></a> Our true competitive advantage lies in the process knowledge embodied by America’s talent. Without skilled practitioners who pass their craft to those who follow, the engine stalls.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-9-zh"><p>论文与专利不是进步的终点，而是培养更好的科学家、工程师和技术人员的途中驿站。科学不只关乎设备——任何有足够资金的实验室都能买到，也不只关乎说明书——一张纸就能传给别人。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-124-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-124" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 124"><sup>124</sup></a> 我们真正的竞争优势，在于体现在美国人才身上的工艺知识。如果没有把技艺传给后来者的熟练从业者，这台发动机就会熄火。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.2 我们的制造基础

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.2 Our Manufacturing Base</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-11-en"><p>America has endured a sustained period of deindustrialization. Manufacturing employment peaked at nearly 20 million workers in 1979;<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-125-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-125" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 125"><sup>125</sup></a> today it stands at roughly 13 million, a decline of around 35%, even as the population has grown by more than 50%.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-126-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-126" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 126"><sup>126</sup></a> Manufacturing’s share of total employment fell from nearly 22% in 1979 to around 8% today.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-127-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-127" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 127"><sup>127</sup></a> This sustained decline has been compounded by the offshoring of contract research and development, especially in the pharmaceutical industry, where laboratories have moved abroad en masse. The fate of the American scientific enterprise is inseparable from the fate of American industry for two reasons.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-11-zh"><p>美国经历了一个持续的去工业化时期。制造业就业在 1979 年达到近 2,000 万人的峰值；<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-125-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-125" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 125"><sup>125</sup></a> 如今约为 1,300 万人，减少约 35%，而同期人口增长了 50% 以上。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-126-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-126" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 126"><sup>126</sup></a> 制造业在总就业中的比重从 1979 年的近 22% 降到今天的约 8%。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-127-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-127" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 127"><sup>127</sup></a> 与此同时，合同研发的离岸外包加剧了这一持续下滑，制药业尤其明显——那里的实验室已大规模迁往海外。美国科学事业的命运与美国产业的命运不可分割，原因有两点。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-12-en"><p>First, most of the economic returns from scientific discovery arise not at the moment of invention, but during the translation of new ideas into products that can be produced at scale. The returns lie in the work that follows invention: the engineering that makes designs manufacturable, the process refinements that bring costs down, the skilled workforce that operates advanced facilities, the supply chain relationships that enable scale. When technological translation moves abroad, so do the jobs, the expertise, and the capacity to produce the next generation of breakthroughs.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-12-zh"><p>第一，科学发现带来的经济回报，大多不产生于发明的那一刻，而产生于把新想法转化为可规模化生产的产品的过程之中。回报存在于发明之后的工作里：让设计变得可制造的工程工作，把成本降下来的工艺改进，操作先进设施的熟练劳动力，支撑规模化的供应链关系。当技术转化移向海外，就业、专长以及生产下一代突破的能力也随之而去。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-13-en"><p>Second, science and production continually inform one another. As discussed in <em>Chapter I</em>, the linear model in which basic research flows neatly to applied research, development, and production has always been a simplification. Knowledge circulates not only between the theorist and the experimentalist, but between the experimentalist and the industrial sector as well. The scientist studying semiconductor physics learns from the manufacturing engineer wrestling with yields. The biologist designing a new therapeutic depends on the process chemist who can scale production. The roboticist developing a high-torque actuator benefits from the presence of a local precision manufacturing base, working where he can drive down the street to stand beside a machinist at the turning center to optimize the design in person.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-13-zh"><p>第二，科学与生产不断相互启发。正如<em>第一章</em>所论，基础研究顺畅地流向应用研究、开发和生产的「线性模型」，一直是一种简化。知识的流动不只在理论家与实验家之间，也在实验家与产业部门之间。研究半导体物理的科学家，从与良率搏斗的制造工程师那里学到东西。设计新疗法的生物学家，依赖能够放大生产规模的工艺化学家。研制高扭矩执行器的机器人专家，受益于本地精密制造基础的存在——他可以开车沿街走一小段路，站到车削中心旁的机械师身边，当面优化设计。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-14-en"><p>These feedback loops depend on proximity between scientific research and industrial capability. Without local manufacturing capacity, the marriage of science and craft weakens. Scientists lose access to the practical problems that inspire new lines of inquiry and improve research quality, while industry loses the research ecosystem that sustains technological leadership. We need to reshore American manufacturing, not only for the sake of fruitful employment, but for the long-term health of American science itself.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-14-zh"><p>这些反馈回路取决于科学研究与工业能力是否彼此邻近。没有本地的制造能力，科学与技艺的联姻就会变弱。科学家失去那些能激发新研究线索、提升研究质量的实际问题，产业则失去支撑技术领先的研究生态。我们需要把美国制造业迁回本土，不仅为了有意义的就业，也为了美国科学自身的长远健康。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.3 巨大的潜力尚未开发

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.3 Vast Potential Remains Untapped</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-16-en"><p>Even after decades of offshoring, the United States still nurtures some of the most dynamic trade communities in the world. Ours is a nation of tinkerers, hobbyists, and people who fix things with their hands. Countless Americans learn to repair cars from family members, to operate power tools, and to build and maintain their own homes. From barn raisings on the frontier to hot rod culture in the 20th century to today’s maker movement, this do-it-yourself (DIY) spirit runs deep in our culture.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-16-zh"><p>即使在数十年的产业外迁之后，美国仍然孕育着世界上一些最有活力的技艺社群。我们是一个由修补匠、业余爱好者和亲手修东西的人组成的国家。无数美国人跟着家人学会修车、使用电动工具、建造并维护自己的房屋。从边疆时代的「搭谷仓」，到 20 世纪的改装车文化，再到今天的创客运动，这种「自己动手」（DIY）的精神深深扎根于我们的文化。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-17-en"><p>Log onto any video sharing platform and you will find a country of builders. Amateur machinists demonstrate techniques for precision manufacturing. Hobbyist welders share tips on joining titanium. Electronics enthusiasts repair broken oscilloscopes. Amateur radio operators, biohackers, synthesizer builders, and drone constructors all participate in communities of shared technical knowledge. Even highly specialized pursuits such as nuclear fusion and cyclotron construction have attracted dedicated experimenters. Public libraries increasingly offer 3D printers and laser cutters, while local shops provide courses in welding and machining.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-17-zh"><p>打开任何一个视频分享平台，你都会看到一个由建设者组成的国家。业余机械师演示精密加工的技法。焊工爱好者分享焊接钛材的窍门。电子爱好者修好坏掉的示波器。业余无线电爱好者、生物黑客、合成器制作者和无人机制作者，都参与到共享技术知识的社群中。就连核聚变、回旋加速器建造这类高度专门化的追求，也吸引了专注的实验者。公共图书馆越来越多地提供 3D 打印机和激光切割机，本地商铺则开设焊接与机加工课程。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-18-en"><p>This grassroots engagement with technical work points to a vast reservoir of talent waiting to be cultivated. More than half of American adults participate in some form of making or building activity.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-128-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-128" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 128"><sup>128</sup></a> The largest DIY conventions have attracted more than a hundred thousand participants.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-129-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-129" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 129"><sup>129</sup></a> Manufacturing employment may have declined, but the cultural foundations of technical skill remain in the same population from which we once drew machinists, toolmakers, and engineers.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-18-zh"><p>这种自下而上的技术参与，说明我们拥有一座尚待开发的人才储备库。超过一半的美国成年人参与某种形式的制作或建造活动。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-128-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-128" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 128"><sup>128</sup></a> 最大的 DIY 展会吸引过十万人以上的参与者。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-129-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-129" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 129"><sup>129</sup></a> 制造业就业也许下降了，但技术技能的文化根基仍然留在同一批人口之中——我们当年正是从这批人中招来机械师、模具工和工程师。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.4 当教育体系让天平倾斜

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.4 As Our Educational System Tilted the Scales</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-20-en"><p>Yet our formal educational and employment systems often fail to develop this potential. Over the past several decades, the expansion of college education has come at the expense of vocational training, and high schools that once taught machining classes have shifted resources toward college preparation. As factories closed and communities hollowed out, the message to young people that working with your hands is a fallback, not a calling, was clear. Success meant escaping physical work, not mastering it.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-20-zh"><p>然而，我们正规的教育与就业体系往往未能开发这一潜力。过去几十年，大学教育的扩张是以职业培训为代价的；曾经开设机加工课的高中，把资源转向了升学准备。随着工厂关闭、社区凋敝，传递给年轻人的信息十分清楚：动手干活是退路，而不是志业。成功意味着逃离体力劳动，而不是精通它。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-21-en"><p>This cultural shift was reinforced by an economic transformation that treated physical labor as a commodity to be sourced wherever it was cheapest. This prejudice runs deep. In too many communities, politicians and guidance counselors have come to treat trade schools as consolation prizes for those not cut out for a four-year degree. Over the past two decades, shop class equipment from shuttered programs has flooded the used machinery market, tangible evidence of how thoroughly we abandoned hands-on education in our rush toward a so-called knowledge economy.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-130-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-130" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 130"><sup>130</sup></a></p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-21-zh"><p>这一文化转变又被一场经济转型所强化：在那场转型中，体力劳动被视为一种商品，哪里最便宜就从哪里采购。这种偏见根深蒂固。在太多的社区里，政治人物和升学顾问已经把职业学校当成给读不了四年制学位的人的安慰奖。过去二十年，被关停课程留下的金工设备涌入二手机械市场——这是我们奔向所谓「知识经济」时把动手教育抛弃得多么彻底的实物证据。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-130-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-130" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 130"><sup>130</sup></a></p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-22-en"><p>The costs are now visible on both sides of the ledger. Millions of Americans have the aptitude and interest for technical work, but lack clear pathways to translate that interest into careers. Meanwhile, millions of skilled jobs are expected to be unfilled even as graduates enter the workforce.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-131-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-131" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 131"><sup>131</sup></a> For decades, the Federal Government tilted the scales against career education by extending unlimited loans to students attending colleges, universities, and graduate programs, driving up the cost of college and burying millions in debt.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-132-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-132" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 132"><sup>132</sup></a> At the root of this policy failure was the government’s inability to recognize that the work of building, maintaining, and repairing the physical world is not a relic of the past, but the foundation of any future prosperity.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-22-zh"><p>代价如今在账本的两侧都看得见。数以百万计的美国人有从事技术工作的天资与兴趣，却缺少把这种兴趣变成职业的清晰通道。与此同时，即便毕业生不断进入劳动力市场，预计仍有数以百万计的技能岗位无人填补。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-131-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-131" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 131"><sup>131</sup></a> 几十年来，联邦政府通过向就读学院、大学和研究生项目的学生提供无上限贷款，把天平压向不利于职业教育的一边，推高了大学成本，也让数百万人背上债务。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-132-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-132" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 132"><sup>132</sup></a> 这一政策失败的根源，是政府没能认识到：建造、维护和修理物质世界的工作不是过去的遗物，而是未来一切繁荣的基础。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.5 必须把科学重构为更宽广的事业

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.5 We Must Restructure Science as a Broader Endeavor</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-24-en"><p>Too many of our universities and elite science and technology curricula have severed the connection between theory and craft. Engineering students study the theory of combustion, but few can disassemble and rebuild a combustion engine. Graduate programs reward theoretical contributions measured in citation counts, but not practical applications measured in jobs and dollars. The result is a generation of researchers who can model phenomena mathematically but cannot repair the apparatus in their own laboratories.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-24-zh"><p>我们太多的大学和精英科技课程割断了理论与技艺之间的联系。工科学生学过燃烧理论，但很少有人能拆开并重新组装一台内燃机。研究生项目奖励以引用次数衡量的理论贡献，却不奖励以就业和经济效益衡量的实际应用。结果是一代研究者能用数学建模描述现象，却修不好自己实验室里的装置。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-25-en"><p>This narrowing departs from how science actually advances. As discussed in <em>Chapter I</em>, the linear model no longer holds in many fields, where discovery increasingly relies on feedback from the real world. Some of the most important breakthroughs in molecular biology and theoretical physics have come from scientists who understood their instruments intimately, who could not only design the experiments but build and modify the equipment themselves.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-25-zh"><p>这种窄化背离了科学实际的推进方式。正如<em>第一章</em>所论，线性模型在许多领域已不再成立，那里的发现越来越依赖来自真实世界的反馈。分子生物学和理论物理学中一些最重要的突破，来自那些对仪器了如指掌的科学家——他们不仅能设计实验，还能自己建造和改造设备。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-26-en"><p>Consider Rainer Weiss, who won the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics for detecting gravitational waves. Weiss grew up scavenging war surplus electronics in New York, teaching himself to build ham radio transmitters and fixing broken devices for pocket money. After flunking out of MIT, he took a job as a laboratory technician, working alongside veteran craftsmen, learning to machine, solder, and weld.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-26-zh"><p>以 Rainer Weiss 为例，他因探测到引力波而获得 2017 年诺贝尔物理学奖。Weiss 在纽约长大，靠捡战后剩余的电子器件自学制作业余无线电发射机，并靠修好坏掉的设备赚零花钱。因成绩不及格离开 MIT 之后，他去做了实验室技术员，与老练的工匠一起工作，学会了机加工、锡焊和焊接。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-27-en"><p>It was this training in what Weiss called “the art of improvisation in experimental science” that enabled him to design and build the prototype laser interferometer that became LIGO, the instrument that detected ripples in spacetime from colliding black holes a billion light-years away. As Weiss put it, “I’m a big believer in what’s called the apprentice system.”<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-133-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-133" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 133"><sup>133</sup></a></p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-27-zh"><p>正是这种被 Weiss 称为「实验科学中即兴创造的艺术」的训练，使他能够设计并建造出后来成为 LIGO 的原型激光干涉仪——这台仪器探测到了十亿光年外黑洞碰撞在时空里激起的涟漪。用 Weiss 的话说：「我非常信奉所谓的学徒制。」<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-133-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-133" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 133"><sup>133</sup></a></p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-28-en"><p>The divorce between scientific training and craft has held back America’s scientific progress. The tacit knowledge that powers our scientific enterprise, developed through experimental practice and hands-on technical training, will only become more important. The particle accelerators at our national laboratories need electrical engineers who can develop more powerful klystrons; fusion experiments need vacuum specialists and fabricators who can work with tungsten; telescopes that map the universe need craftsmen who grind mirrors to nanometer precision. These are the people who may well be core contributors to the next technological breakthrough. We must give STEM students at every level of study the opportunity for hands-on technical training, and conversely, ensure America’s skilled technical workforce has clear pathways to participate in formal academic training and scientific research. The glorification of craft, industry, and manufacturing that once characterized American culture must be revived, and we will be richer for it.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-28-zh"><p>科学训练与技艺之间的分离，拖累了美国的科学进步。驱动我们科学事业的默会知识——经由实验实践和动手技术训练积累而来——只会变得越来越重要。我们国家实验室的粒子加速器，需要有能研制更强大速调管的电气工程师；聚变实验需要有能处理钨材料的真空专家和制造人员；绘制宇宙的望远镜需要有能把镜面磨到纳米级精度的工匠。这些人很可能就是下一项技术突破的核心贡献者。我们必须让各学习阶段的 STEM 学生都有接受动手技术训练的机会；反过来，也要确保美国的技能型技术劳动力有清晰通道参与正规学术训练与科学研究。我们必须重新树立起曾经作为美国文化特征的那种对手艺、产业和制造的尊崇，我们也会因此更加富足。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="stat">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-29-en"><p>1 in 3 Americans live in a county with no R&amp;D employer</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-29-zh"><p>每 3 个美国人中就有 1 人所在的县没有任何研发雇主</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.6 通过扩大参与

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.6 Through Expanding Participation</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-31-en"><p>Our model of scientific training must adapt in three ways: by incorporating technical training, breaking academic credentialism, and connecting grassroots learning to formal scientific research.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-31-zh"><p>我们的科学训练模式必须在三个方面作出调整：纳入技术训练、打破学术文凭主义，以及把基层学习与正规科学研究连接起来。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-32-en"><p>First, we must reconnect university science and engineering programs with hands-on, practical knowledge. This requires integrating technical training into university curricula, breaking down barriers between “elite” and “vocational” schooling, and reforming accreditation to reward real-world technical work, which would include counting hands-on externships and registered apprenticeship hours toward accredited degrees. Those who set curricula across the country should think seriously about what a world of more abundant intelligence and more constrained craft knowledge means for the expertise most required by the next generation.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-32-zh"><p>第一，我们必须让大学的科学与工程课程重新与实践性的动手知识建立联系。这要求把技术训练纳入大学课程，打破「精英」教育与「职业」教育之间的壁垒，并改革认证制度以奖励真实世界的技术工作——包括把动手实习（externship）和注册学徒工时计入受认证的学位。全国制定课程的人应当认真思考：在一个智能更充裕、技艺知识却更受限的世界里，下一代最需要的专长是什么。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-33-en"><p>Second, we must create new pathways into our scientific enterprise grounded in demonstrated skill rather than academic pedigree alone. Today, the conventional academic ladder is the only widely legible route into research. We must lay alternative paths that allow more makers, crafters, and technicians to participate in academic training and scientific discovery if they choose to do so. National fellowships could place skilled machinists and lab technicians at national labs and research universities, with skill-based pathways to credentials and co-authorship on research outputs. Practitioners-in-residence programs, analogous to artists-in-residence, could embed experienced craftsmen alongside Ph.D. researchers, granting them access to specialized equipment, professional mentorship, and attention for their research without requiring a doctorate. National laboratories could develop portable, industry-recognized credentials in areas like cryogenics and advanced machining. Programs like SBIR open doors for technician-founded ventures, directing resources toward ideas that do not always start with a dissertation.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-33-zh"><p>第二，我们必须开辟以实际技能、而非仅以学术出身为基础进入科学事业的新通道。今天，常规的学术阶梯是唯一一条被普遍理解的进入研究工作的路径。我们必须铺设替代路径，让更多的制作者、手艺人和技术员在愿意时能够参与学术训练与科学发现。国家奖学金可以把熟练的机械师和实验室技术员安置到国家实验室和研究型大学，并为他们提供以技能为基础的取得资质、在研究产出上署名合著的通道。「驻场实践者」计划类似驻场艺术家，可以把有经验的工匠与博士研究者安置在一起，让他们无需博士学位就能使用专门设备、获得专业指导，并让自己的研究得到关注。国家实验室可以开发在低温技术、先进机加工等领域可携带、被行业认可的资质证书。SBIR 之类的计划为技术员创办的企业打开大门，把资源导向那些并不总是始于博士论文的想法。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-34-en"><p>Third, we must connect the millions of Americans who tinker, fabricate, and repair to engineering and research. This is especially critical for rural students, who face distinct challenges in accessing traditional academic pathways. They are less likely to have family members working in STEM fields. Their schools receive less outreach from industry. The smaller populations in their towns make it harder to find like-minded peers. And yet many of our best scientists and engineers first learned to weld in a barn, or helped their families fix tractors growing up. The answer is not to pluck talented individuals from their communities, but to bring the frontier to them, creating more connection points between maker culture and our formal science enterprise.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-34-zh"><p>第三，我们必须把数以百万计的修补、制作和修理东西的美国人，与工程和研究连接起来。这对农村学生尤为关键，他们在进入传统学术通道时面临独特的困难。他们的家人更少有人在 STEM 领域工作。他们的学校较少有产业界前来开展活动。他们所在的小镇人口更少，更难找到志同道合的同龄人。然而我们许多最优秀的科学家和工程师，最早是在谷仓里学会焊接的，或者小时候帮家里修过拖拉机。答案不是把有才华的人从他们的社区里拔走，而是把前沿带到他们身边，在创客文化与我们的正规科学事业之间创造更多连接点。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.7 一体化的培养模式

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.7 Integrated Models of Training</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-36-en"><p>To sustain America’s scientific leadership, we must rebuild integrated communities from community colleges to extension systems to keep the frontier of science and technology open not only to a select few, but to every American who has the aptitude and interest to advance it.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-36-zh"><p>为了维持美国的科学领导地位，我们必须重建从社区学院到推广体系的一体化社群，让科学技术的前沿不仅向少数人开放，也向每一位有天赋、有兴趣去推进它的美国人开放。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-37-en"><p>Community colleges are the natural foundation for scaling scientific and technical training. Congress has provided major funding to these institutions in recent years, and justifiably so. They enroll around 40% of all undergraduates and serve as the primary entry point to higher education for first-generation students, veterans, and working adults.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-134-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-134" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 134"><sup>134</sup></a> They also provide apprentices with Related Technical Instruction in classrooms, pairing theory with on-the-job training.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-37-zh"><p>社区学院是扩大科学与技术训练规模的天然基础。近年来国会为这些机构提供了大笔资金，这是有道理的。它们招收了约 40% 的本科生，并且是第一代大学生、退伍军人和在职成年人进入高等教育的主要入口。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-134-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-134" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 134"><sup>134</sup></a> 它们还在课堂上为学徒提供「相关技术教学」，把理论与在职训练结合起来。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-38-en"><p>With targeted support, community colleges can become regional hubs for scientific and technological innovation, integrating with critical industries, NSF Regional Innovation Engines, and local ecosystem initiatives. These partnerships can channel shared facility access, equipment donations, and industry-led, co-developed curricula into institutions that already train America’s best technical talent. The Trump Administration has made expanding apprenticeships a priority, directing federal agencies to reach and surpass one million active apprenticeships annually. The Department of Labor (DOL) has shifted toward a pay-for-performance model, replacing traditional upfront grants for employer-led apprenticeships with funding tied to apprentice hiring and retention.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-135-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-135" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 135"><sup>135</sup></a> And with the passage of Workforce Pell in 2025, short-term training programs are, for the first time, eligible for Pell Grant funding.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-38-zh"><p>有了有针对性的支持，社区学院可以成为区域科技创新枢纽，与关键产业、NSF 区域创新引擎以及本地生态计划整合起来。这些伙伴关系可以把共享设施的使用权、设备捐赠和产业界主导、共同开发的课程，输送到那些已经在培养美国最优秀技术人才的机构。Trump 政府把扩大学徒制列为优先事项，要求联邦机构每年达到并超过 100 万个在册学徒岗位。劳工部（DOL）已转向按绩效付费的模式，用与学徒录用和留任挂钩的资金，取代过去为雇主主导的学徒制提供的预先拨款。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-135-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-135" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 135"><sup>135</sup></a> 随着 2025 年「劳动力佩尔助学金」（Workforce Pell）的通过，短期培训项目首次有资格获得佩尔助学金资助。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-39-en"><p>Going further, we could extend registered apprenticeships into fields that have not traditionally used them, particularly in science and technology. These shifts move us toward a more practical system of education that restores integrated mentorship and embeds learning in real-world application.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-136-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-136" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 136"><sup>136</sup></a> And to ensure scientific opportunity is not limited by geography, training must be distributed nationwide. Programs like the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Cooperative Extension System could expand its remit to include critical sciences and technologies, creating strongholds in rural areas. Employers who most need skilled workers could partner with nearby community colleges by donating equipment and supporting instruction. These programs should serve as entry points into a broader regional innovation ecosystem, helping young talent network with mentors and peers who can channel their entrepreneurial energy into shared projects.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-39-zh"><p>更进一步，我们可以把注册学徒制延伸到传统上不使用它的领域，尤其是科学与技术领域。这些转变把我们推向一种更务实的教育体系：恢复一体化的师徒指导，并把学习嵌入真实世界的应用中。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-136-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-136" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 136"><sup>136</sup></a> 为确保科学机会不受地理限制，训练必须在全国范围内分布。美国农业部的合作推广体系这类项目，可以扩大其职责范围，把关键科学与技术纳入其中，在农村地区建立据点。最需要技能型员工的雇主可以与附近的社区学院合作，捐赠设备、支持教学。这些项目应当成为进入更广泛区域创新生态的入口，帮助年轻人才与能够把他们的创业能量引导到共同项目中的导师和同伴建立联系。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.8 以及新的转化路径

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.8 And New Paths for Translation</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-41-en"><p>American technological leadership has repeatedly emerged from regional clusters where research and production were inseparable. In the early 20th century, Detroit became the world’s automotive capital not merely because of Ford’s factories, but because a dense ecosystem of suppliers, machinists, and engineering talent made the region uniquely capable of translating automotive innovations into mass production. Thousands of small suppliers could prototype and manufacture new components faster than anywhere else on earth.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-137-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-137" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 137"><sup>137</sup></a></p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-41-zh"><p>美国的技术领先一再产生于研究与生产密不可分的区域集群。20 世纪初，底特律成为世界汽车之都，不仅因为 Ford 的工厂，更因为那里密集的供应商、机械师和工程人才生态，使该地区拥有把汽车创新转化为大规模生产的独特能力。成千上万家小供应商试制和制造新零件的速度，地球上任何地方都比不上。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-137-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-137" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 137"><sup>137</sup></a></p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-42-en"><p>Such clusters work because they create dense connections among industrial production, scientific research, and a skilled technical workforce.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-138-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-138" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 138"><sup>138</sup></a> The model persists today, where different regions specialize in distinct domains, such as optics in Arizona, biotechnology in the Boston corridor, aerospace in Colorado and Alabama, and advanced manufacturing in the Midwest. In these clusters, knowledge accumulates locally and is reinforced by a culture of practical problem-solving that emerges between the skilled technical workforce and dense supplier networks.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-42-zh"><p>这类集群之所以有效，是因为它们在工业生产、科学研究和技能型技术劳动力之间建立起密集的联系。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-138-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-138" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 138"><sup>138</sup></a> 这一模式延续至今：不同地区专精于不同领域，比如亚利桑那的光学、波士顿走廊的生物技术、科罗拉多和亚拉巴马州的航空航天，以及中西部的先进制造。在这些集群中，知识在本地积累，并被技能型技术劳动力与密集供应商网络之间形成的那种务实解决问题的文化不断强化。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-43-en"><p>As the United States offshored manufacturing, it also severed these connections and the process knowledge they sustain. For too long, America’s leaders assumed that we could retain high-value design work while ceding production. But as competitors began to manufacture at scale, they improved their ability to design and iterate. Vice President Vance captured this dynamic precisely, observing that over time, “the geographies that do the manufacturing get awfully good at the designing of things.”<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-139-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-139" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 139"><sup>139</sup></a></p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-43-zh"><p>当美国把制造业转向海外时，也切断了这些联系以及它们所承载的工艺知识。长期以来，美国领导人以为我们可以在让出生产的同时保留高价值的设计工作。但当竞争者开始大规模制造时，他们设计与迭代的能力也随之提高。Vance 副总统准确地概括了这一动态：随着时间推移，「从事制造的地区会变得极其擅长设计东西。」<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-139-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-139" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 139"><sup>139</sup></a></p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-44-en"><p>Recent federal initiatives have taken early steps toward reversing this trend and rebuilding America’s innovation clusters. The NSF’s Regional Innovation Engines and the Commerce Department’s Tech Hubs channel resources to stimulate place-based production ecosystems outside traditional coastal hubs. Programs such as the Manufacturing USA Institutes, NIST’s Manufacturing Extension Partnership, and DOW’s eight Microelectronic Commons regional hubs further incentivize industry partnerships, open shared R&amp;D infrastructure, and drive industry-led workforce training. These clusters lower the barrier for small manufacturers to create new products, test applications of new technologies, and build a manufacturing workforce with the skills of the future. Whole-of-government industrial policy reinforces this shift, driving increased demand for American-made products and changing the calculus for where companies manufacture. The Federal Government is using innovative economic tools to attract investment commitments from foreign governments, and so financing American production, training American workers, and building American supply chains.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-44-zh"><p>最近的联邦举措已迈出初步步伐，试图扭转这一趋势、重建美国的创新集群。NSF 的「区域创新引擎」和商务部的「技术枢纽」投入资源，刺激传统沿海枢纽之外地方性的生产生态。Manufacturing USA 研究所、NIST 的「制造业扩展伙伴关系」以及战争部（DOW）的八个「微电子共享」区域枢纽等项目，进一步激励产业伙伴关系、开放共享研发基础设施，并推动产业界主导的劳动力培训。这些集群降低了小型制造商开发新产品、测试新技术应用并建设具备未来技能的制造劳动力的门槛。全政府范围的产业政策强化了这一转变，推动对美国制造产品的需求上升，并改变企业选择在何处制造的考量。联邦政府正在运用创新性的经济工具，争取外国政府作出投资承诺，从而为美国的生产融资、培训美国工人、建设美国供应链。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-45-en"><p>That said, the Federal Government cannot build these ecosystems alone. State and local governments hold critical levers, including land use and permitting, education and workforce development, anchor institutions, and more, which enable them to cultivate competitive advantages. Done poorly, such competition can become a race to the bottom that transfers public money to mobile firms, but done well, smart policies can cultivate long-lasting regional ecosystems. By leveraging the benefits of federalism, the United States can pursue parallel experimentation where 50 states and thousands of localities experiment with different approaches to cultivating industry clusters, competing to attract investment and talent.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-45-zh"><p>话虽如此，联邦政府无法独自建成这些生态。州和地方政府掌握着关键杠杆，包括土地使用与许可、教育与劳动力发展、锚定机构等等，这使它们能够培育竞争优势。做得不好，这种竞争会变成一场竞相压价的恶性竞赛，把公共资金转移给可以随时搬迁的企业；做得好，聪明的政策能培育出长久的区域生态。利用联邦制的好处，美国可以开展并行试验：50 个州和数千个地方各自尝试培育产业集群的不同做法，竞相吸引投资和人才。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-46-en"><p>Several state-led efforts illustrate the approach. When new semiconductor fabrication plants were announced in New Albany, Ohio, the state committed roughly $2 billion in incentives spanning direct cash “onshoring incentive grants,” infrastructure spending, and job creation tax credits.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-140-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-140" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 140"><sup>140</sup></a> A community college in Columbus now leads a statewide <a href="https://www.cscc.edu/about/news/2022/intel-groundbreaking-sept-22.shtml">network</a> of 23 Ohio colleges developing open, shareable curricula for a two-year degree pathway into chip manufacturing technician careers.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-141-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-141" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 141"><sup>141</sup></a> A semiconductor company has invested <a href="https://engineering.osu.edu/news/2022/03/intel-announces-50-million-investment-ohio-higher-education">$50 million</a> in Ohio higher education to support comprehensive semiconductor workforce development, spanning curriculum development, faculty training, reskilling and upskilling programs, work-based learning, and laboratory equipment upgrades, multiply federal dollars from NSF.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-142-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-142" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 142"><sup>142</sup></a> In Taylor, Texas, state-led support for semiconductor manufacturing helped attract a nearly $5 billion capital investment supporting thousands of high-quality jobs.<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-143-en" href="#fn-chapter-04-143" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 143"><sup>143</sup></a> Across these cases, state leaders have treated industrial development as a core priority, aligning local government, educational institutions, and industry on workforce development. As localities experiment, the most successful will discover models others can adapt.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-46-zh"><p>若干州主导的做法体现了这一思路。当新的半导体工厂宣布落户俄亥俄州 New Albany 时，该州承诺了约 20 亿美元的激励措施，涵盖直接现金的「回流激励补助」、基础设施支出和创造就业税收抵免。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-140-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-140" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 140"><sup>140</sup></a> 哥伦布的一所社区学院如今牵头一个由俄亥俄州 23 所院校组成的全州<a href="https://www.cscc.edu/about/news/2022/intel-groundbreaking-sept-22.shtml">网络</a>，为通往芯片制造技术员职业的两年制学位路径开发开放、可共享的课程。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-141-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-141" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 141"><sup>141</sup></a> 一家半导体公司向俄亥俄州高等教育投入了 <a href="https://engineering.osu.edu/news/2022/03/intel-announces-50-million-investment-ohio-higher-education">5,000 万美元</a>，支持全面的半导体人才队伍建设，涵盖课程开发、师资培训、再培训与技能提升项目、基于工作的学习以及实验室设备升级，使 NSF 的联邦资金产生倍增效应。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-142-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-142" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 142"><sup>142</sup></a> 在德克萨斯州 Taylor，州主导的半导体制造支持帮助吸引了近 50 亿美元的资本投资，支撑数千个高质量岗位。<a class="noteref" id="fnref-chapter-04-143-zh" href="#fn-chapter-04-143" role="doc-noteref" title="脚注 143"><sup>143</sup></a> 在这些案例中，州领导人把产业发展当作核心优先事项，使地方政府、教育机构与产业界在劳动力发展上保持一致。随着各地展开试验，最成功的做法将形成可供他人借鉴的模式。</p></div>
</div>
```

## IV.9 让进步惠及所有人

```{=html}
<div class="en h-en"><p>IV.9 To Make Progress Available to All</p></div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-48-en"><p>American innovation has never been confined to elite university laboratories. In a local workshop, hobbyists young and old work together to retrofit a Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machine to wind carbon-overwrapped pressure vessels. At a private airstrip on the East Coast, a defense technology startup has pitched a trailer at the end of the field, experimenting with new propellant mixtures. Out in the mesas of the New Mexico desert, a student tinkers in a rusty shed, trying to harness the power of the sun through an inertial confinement fusion device cobbled together from laboratory surplus. Innovation advances in these places, far from major research campuses, through hands-on experimentation, the accumulation of craft knowledge, and a bias toward action.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-48-zh"><p>美国的创新从来不局限于精英大学的实验室。在某个本地工坊里，老老少少的爱好者一起改装一台计算机数控（CNC）机床，用来缠绕碳纤维外覆的压力容器。在东海岸的一处私人简易机场，一家国防技术创业公司在场地尽头搭起拖车，试验新的推进剂配方。在新墨西哥沙漠的台地之间，一名学生在生锈的棚屋里捣鼓，试图用实验室剩余物资拼凑起来的惯性约束聚变装置驾驭太阳能。创新就在这些远离大型研究校园的地方推进——靠动手实验、技艺知识的积累，以及一种行动优先的倾向。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-49-en"><p>If this tradition is to endure, we must build a future in which entrepreneurship is not confined by geography or credentials, in which a student in a rural town, a machinist in a small city, and a researcher at a major university each has pathways to contribute to technological progress. A future in which science is not gated by pedigree, but open to all with aptitude and drive. The falling costs of computational power, manufacturing equipment, and scientific tools make this increasingly possible, placing capabilities once reserved for major corporations in the hands of small businesses, community colleges, and individual tinkerers.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-49-zh"><p>如果这一传统要延续下去，我们必须建设这样一个未来：创业不受地理或文凭的限制，农村小镇的学生、小城市的机械师和重点大学的研究者都有为技术进步作贡献的通道；科学不由出身把关，而向所有有天赋、有干劲的人开放。算力、制造设备和科学工具成本的下降，使这一点越来越可能实现——曾经只有大企业才拥有的能力，正在落到小企业、社区学院和个体修补匠手中。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-50-en"><p>Alongside new pathways to contribute to the scientific enterprise, this future will create pathways for all to experience the benefits of scientific and technological progress. In the past, the integration of science and craft has produced entirely new markets, industries, and forms of work. Aircraft mechanics, modern welding, CNC machining, and semiconductor manufacturing emerged as skilled crafts in the 20th century; none existed a generation before. Each required its own body of tacit knowledge, its own communities of practice, and its own ties to science and engineering. Each created dignified work for millions of Americans and sustained entire communities. We should expect the same from the technologies taking shape today, but only if we make broad participation possible.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-50-zh"><p>在开辟为科学事业作贡献的新通道的同时，这一未来也会为所有人创造享受科技进步成果的通道。过去，科学与技艺的结合催生了全新的市场、产业和工作形态。航空器机械师、现代焊接、CNC 加工和半导体制造，都是 20 世纪出现的技能手艺；在一代人之前，它们都还不存在。每一种都需要自己的默会知识体系、自己的实践社群，以及自己与科学和工程的纽带。每一种都为数百万美国人创造了有尊严的工作，并养活了整个社区。我们应当期待今天正在成形的技术带来同样的结果——但前提是我们让广泛参与成为可能。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-51-en"><p>Rebuilding our industrial commons is not the work of a single administration. The clusters that once defined American industry took generations to build, and only years to hollow out when production moved overseas. Meeting this moment requires revitalizing the web of skills, suppliers, and tacit knowledge that form America’s industrial commons, and cultivating vibrant communities of scientists, researchers, and craftspeople in a hundred Silicon Valleys across the nation.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-51-zh"><p>重建我们的工业公地不是一届政府的事。曾定义美国产业的那些集群，用了好几代人才建成，而生产一旦移往海外，只用了几年就被掏空。应对当下，需要重振构成美国工业公地的技能、供应商与默会知识之网，并在全国上百个「硅谷」培育由科学家、研究者和手艺人组成的充满活力的社群。</p></div>
</div>
<div class="pair">
<div class="en" id="p-chapter-04-52-en"><p>The triumphs of American science and technology have never been the work of any singular locale, and have always drawn on distributed strengths. The Manhattan Project pulled talent from across the country, including physicists from Berkeley, engineers from Tennessee, and craftsmen from New Mexico. The space program employed hundreds of thousands in facilities spread across multiple states, from Houston to Huntsville to Cape Canaveral. The agricultural modernization that multiplied farm productivity in the mid-20th century was driven by land-grant universities and extension agents serving communities in every corner of the nation. Throughout our history, American scientific genius has been broad-based and open to all, and it must remain so.</p></div>
<div class="zh" id="p-chapter-04-52-zh"><p>美国科学与技术的辉煌从来不是某一个地方的功劳，而始终汲取着分布在全国的力量。曼哈顿计划从全国各地汇聚人才，包括来自伯克利的物理学家、来自田纳西的工程师和来自新墨西哥的工匠。太空计划在横跨多州的设施中雇用了数十万人，从休斯敦到亨茨维尔再到卡纳维拉尔角。20 世纪中叶使农业生产力成倍增长的农业现代化，靠的是赠地大学和推广人员服务于全国每一个角落的社区。纵观我们的历史，美国的科学天才都是广泛分布的、向所有人开放的，而且必须继续如此。</p></div>
</div>
```
